summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with mast cell degranulation syndrome was admitted for a recurrent mast cell flare characterized by chest pain, shortness of breath, itching, abdominal pain, and nausea, following a recent discharge for similar symptoms. She was treated with intravenous diphenhydramine, hydromorphone, and lorazepam on her usual every-four-hour protocol, with symptomatic relief. Her course was marked by relapsing symptoms despite stable vital signs and no evidence of infection or cardiac ischemia. A chest X-ray showed stable findings with known nodular opacities, and biopsy results from a prior admission confirmed organizing pneumonia without malignancy, which was reassuring. She remained hemodynamically stable, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home after a safety delay post-IV medication administration. Follow-up was arranged with pulmonology and rheumatology to discuss lung nodule management and potential restart of etanercept, with no changes to her home medications.
